…ethane cold-trapped at a winter pole and processed in place, as on Charon's red pole (Grundy et al. 2016). The supply can come from a neighbour's escaping air. Its reddening depends on peak summer temperature (Raut et al. 2022; Gimar et al. 2026).
| Grundy et al. 2016, Nature 539, 65. doi:10.1038/nature19340 | Charon's red pole | found |

- **Mechanism.** Methane escaping Pluto freezes onto Charon's winter pole, which stays very cold through long seasons at high obliquity. Radiation converts it to heavier, less volatile molecules that survive the next sunrise (Grundy et al. 2016).
